caseStudy.title: Awaa Braids
caseStudy.tag: Mobile web app · Product design & build
caseStudy.cardDesc: Book braids from your phone: pick a style, choose a time that's really free, and the salon confirms it.
caseStudy.subtitle: A phone-first booking app for a braiding salon in the Washington, DC area, for customers and the salon itself.

shots.alt: Customer home: the next appointment, with status, stylist and price
Styles and prices, with sizes and lengths
The salon's day: appointments, requests and the week in numbers

caseStudy.overview:
Braiding appointments take hours, and many salons still book them through phone calls and direct messages. Awaa Braids lets customers pick a style, see an honest starting price and how long it takes, and request a time that is really free. The salon sees its day at a glance and confirms requests from a phone.

It is built in five milestones. The first one, the foundation, is live: the front page, sign-in, the customer's appointments, the salon's Today screen, and the database with its security rules.

process.intro: I started from the rules, not the screens: what a booking needs to be fair to the customer and safe for the salon, written and tested in the database first.
steps: Brief: two roles (customer and salon), the booking rules (hours, notice, cancelling, no double-booking) and a phone-first flow.
Data model and security: styles with size and length options, stylists with hours and time off, appointments; Row Level Security and 54 database checks.
Demo salon with fictional people, using the same visibility rules as the database.
Customer and salon screens, tested in the browser at phone, tablet and laptop widths.
Moved to the DC area: US dollars and Eastern Time, with daylight saving handled.

caseStudy.problem: Booking braids by phone call or DM is slow for both sides: the price depends on size and length, a style can take four to six hours, and the stylist's day fills up in uneven blocks. Customers wait for replies and guess at prices; the salon keeps the diary in its head or on paper and risks double-booking.

caseStudy.insight: For braids, the price and the time are the booking. Showing both up front, for the size and length you pick, removes most of the back-and-forth before anyone talks.

caseStudy.solution: A phone-first web app with two sides. Customers see each style with its starting price and time, then their next, upcoming and past appointments with status and price. The salon sees today's appointments with each customer's phone number, the requests waiting and the week in numbers. Booking runs on the server, which works out the price and time from the style and refuses anything outside the rules, including double-booking.

caseStudy.outcome: Milestone 1 is live on Vercel with a demo anyone can try: the front page, sign-in, the customer's appointments and the salon's day, backed by 54 database security checks, 34 unit tests and browser tests at four widths. Next: the booking flow and cancelling, then the salon's tools.
